content.text:
Submitted successfully.

**Repair made for the deterministic failure:** the operative sentence now uses the plain permissive formulation the checklist element is written in — "Ono **may terminate** this Agreement **for convenience at any time**, for any reasons, upon **thirty (30) days' prior written notice** to Array … **in which case Array shall refund on a pro rata basis any prepaid fees** for the period after the effective date of such termination." The earlier "shall have the right to terminate" construction was replaced so the Customer-convenience-termination language is unambiguous on its face.

**Final position — deviation, cured at preferred level with one replace in Section 13.2:**
1. Customer convenience right — delayed commencement tied to First Commercial Sale deleted; right exercisable at any time.
2. Notice — redacted period fixed at 30 days' prior written notice.
3. Refund — express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period.
4. No Vendor convenience right — already met; Article 13 read in full gives Array only for-cause exits (13.3, 13.4), with 13.5 running to Ono alone.

Retained verbatim: the heading, "for any reasons," and the rationale-with-notice requirement. Untouched: 13.1 term and post-expiry licence conversion, 13.3–13.5, Section 8.2, and the Article 14 wind-down mechanics. One negotiator note carried in the rationale: confirm that "prepaid fees" captures the intended upfront/milestone amounts under this licence's economics.
